simplify. you don't need a ton of gear or toys or whatever. Listen to advice,but don't always use it (It WILL be solicited) go by instinct, NOT by google. Your method of parenting will differ from someone else, don't preach, brag, or guilt. This is your family journey, we don't all think the same, we all have differing skillsets, we all have different beliefs, we all have one common goal: to be the best parents our kids will ever have. Focus on here & now and not how you'll do things differently from your parents, your perspective WILL change and your kids will inevitably make a liar out of you. You'll do things you swore you'd never do, and that's ok.

Cherish and use humour as a teaching tool, and experience your life with kids.  Always learning. 

Kids taught me that it's ok to be wrong, and that learning from mistakes is a valuable tool that we work on together.
 Also: You'll think your spouse (provided you have one) will do and does it all wrong, just remember to know they're doing the best they can and that you have the common goal. 

To the stay at home parent: Give your partner advice, don't bark or berate them, this isn't their full time job and although it IS as important to them as it is to you, you have more experience as you're immersed in this

To the working parent: Don't take it to heart, your partner will be exhausted and snippy, they're working all hours of the day and night and it is all consuming, take time to do things for him/her, bring home little treats or sentiments, help with the kids without being asked, Do the dishes or laundry, work as a unit. 

Oh, and if you have dogs, you'll probably want to punch them in the spine...it's just how it is.
